records.name: Philadelphia Dance Company (PHILADANCO!)
records.summary: A professional dance company that performs in Philadelphia, run alongside a dance school for children and adults. The school teaches ballet, modern, jazz, tap and hip hop.
records.what_you_do: Take a class at The Philadelphia School of Dance Arts, for ages 4 and up plus adults, or come see a company show. A show called Danco on Danco is listed for October 10 and 11, 2026.

schedule.text: Studio hours at the West Philadelphia school are Monday to Friday 4 to 9 pm and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm. Class times are not on the site, so call to ask.

locations.label: West Philadelphia studios (Philadelphia School of Dance Arts)
West Oak Lane studio (Philadelphia School of Dance Arts)

cost.text: Tuition is not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Call (215) 387-8202 to ask about open class spots and times, then sign up for a class or buy a ticket to a show.
first_step.basis: The school offers classes for beginners through advanced students and for adults, and it directs people to call for details, though it does not describe a drop-in day.

records.notes: The school page gives (215) 387-8202 for class questions, but the West Oak Lane number shown there, (215) 424-9811, links to the first number, so confirm before calling. Dance education, arts education and community pages had no class details. The events page gives October 10 and 11 for Danco on Danco, while the description names October 11 at 7 pm, so check the date before going.

records.name: Philadelphia Dance Projects
records.notes: Public role found: attend the DANCE UP CLOSE performance series (no dates or ticket details on the site), donate, and follow online. Dance TAG and the school residencies work with teaching artists and schools. The local history and Old City projects were linked but not fetched directly, and the homepage did not say whether the public can join them. No public class, workshop, membership, volunteer or community program was found, so the verdict is not_a_group under the brief. Revisit if the owner counts attend-only presenters as publish, or if the linked project pages show public programs.

records.name: Power of Paint Art Academy and Management
records.summary: A nonprofit art academy that teaches painting to children in paid workshops and runs paint parties. It describes its approach as trauma-informed arts education for young people and their communities.
records.what_you_do: Sign a child up for a multi-week painting workshop (you pay to reserve a spot), book a paint party, or apply to volunteer through the online form on the volunteer page. The volunteer form includes a background check.

schedule.text: Multi-week children's workshops. The site's course descriptions give 10 sessions for the 5-week course and 20 sessions for the 10-week course, each 2 hours. Dates and times are not on the site.

locations.label: Art academy (address from IRS listing, not shown on site)

cost.text: Children's workshops are listed at $650 (5-week) and $1,300 (10-week), paid to reserve. Paint party prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Email help@popartacademy.org or use the contact form on the site to ask about the next children's workshop and whether adults can join. For volunteering, use the application form linked from the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Workshops can be reserved online and volunteer applications are open, but the site does not say whether adults can join or whether drop-ins are welcome.

records.notes: The site footer reads 2018 and no dated news from 2026 was found, only grant badges and a 2025 to 2026 funders list, so recent activity is unclear. The class descriptions do not match their titles. The address comes from the IRS listing in our batch, not the site. The summer camp, afterschool and Art Academy pages are linked but were not read. The volunteer page lists no phone or email.

records.name: The Unscripted Project
records.summary: An improv nonprofit that uses improv games to build speaking, teamwork and confidence in young people. It runs free improv workshops in Philadelphia public school classrooms and a free afterschool improv program for high school students.
records.what_you_do: Philadelphia high school students in grades 9 to 12 can apply for the free Tuesday afterschool improv program at CEG Studios this fall. Adults 18 and up can volunteer to help in school classes. Public schools can request a free 10-week improv workshop for their classes.

schedule.text: Afterschool improv runs Tuesdays, 4 to 7 pm, from September 15 to December 15, 2026. Classroom workshops run during the school day for about 10 weeks.

cost.text: Free for students. Students who finish the full semester get a $100 stipend. Snacks and a light dinner are provided.

first_step.how: Fill in the application form linked on the afterschool page. Spaces are limited. If you are 18 or older, use the volunteer interest form on the volunteer page instead.
first_step.basis: The afterschool program needs an application, spaces are limited, and priority goes to students who finished the in-school program.

records.notes: The homepage news ends in September 2024 and its footer reads 2022, but the afterschool page lists Fall 2026 dates, so the group looks active. Questions about the afterschool go to ellie@unscriptedproject.org, the address published on that page. The 24 to 25 annual report PDF was linked but not read. The in-school program has no public address.

records.name: The Woodlands Trust for Historic Preservation
records.summary: A historic cemetery and garden at 4000 Woodland Avenue. It runs public tours, a public events calendar, and volunteer work days where people clean paths, plant and care for trees, and help welcome visitors.
records.what_you_do: Book a tour of the mansion and cemetery ($20 a person), join a public event such as a walk or an evening event, or sign up for a clean-up or tree day. The Grave Gardeners program, run by The Woodlands, opens applications each January.

schedule.text: Public tours run on weekdays from April through October and last about 1.5 hours. Clean-up work days are on weekends from October to March and on weekday evenings from April to September. Public events are on the calendar.

cost.text: Public tours are $20 per person, with a $5 add-on for lunch setup. Some events are for members only, and other event prices vary.

first_step.how: Request a tour through the online form on the tours page (book at least 2 weeks ahead), or check the volunteer page and join a clean-up work day.
first_step.basis: Tours and public events are open to anyone who books or signs up, but the volunteer page does not spell out a general sign-up process.

records.notes: Grave Gardeners (http://www.gravegardeners.org) is The Woodlands' own volunteer program, with more than 150 volunteers and applications each January. It was checked and folded into this record, not listed separately. Some events are members only. The calendar page does not show when it was captured, so the October 2026 listings are the newest evidence. Tour times are not published, and the tours run seasonally.

records.name: thINKingDANCE
records.summary: A group of dance artists and writers that publishes reviews, essays and news about dance. It is run as a nonprofit and accepts writing from outside writers.
records.what_you_do: Read the reviews and essays on the site, join the mailing list, or send a piece of dance writing through the writer submissions page. You can also support the group with a donation.

schedule.text: New pieces were posted several times in the first week of October 2026.

first_step.how: Read a few recent pieces at thinkingdance.net, then use the writer submissions page to send in a review or essay, or join the mailing list.
first_step.basis: Anyone can read the site, and the writer submissions page explains how to contribute, though the site does not describe how pieces are chosen.

records.notes: Mostly an online publication and writers group, so its public roles are reading, writing and giving. It is published because a Philadelphia-based dance writers group can be joined through writer submissions. If the owner treats online publications as outside the directory, flip this to not_a_group. The homepage does not state a Philadelphia focus; the Philadelphia link comes from our batch address (4815 Regent St). The contact page (https://thinkingdance.net/contact/) and the giving circle page on Grapevine were linked but not read. No address or phone is published.

records.name: United Caribbean Association of Philadelphia (Philly Carnival)
records.summary: The nonprofit behind the Philadelphia Caribbean Carnival. Its costumed mas band, Philly Mas United, is signing people up for the 2027 Carnival.
records.what_you_do: Join Philly Mas United, the band that will play in the 2027 Carnival. Pre-register with the online form on the site. No payment is needed to sign up, and no matching costume is required, so you can use an older costume or make a new one.

schedule.text: The band is planning for the 2027 Philadelphia Caribbean Carnival. Practice dates and times are not listed on the site.

cost.text: No payment is needed to pre-register. Costume and band fees are not listed.

first_step.how: Fill in the pre-registration form linked from the Philly Mas United page on the Carnival site. No payment is needed to sign up.
first_step.basis: Anyone can pre-register online at no cost, but the page does not say what band practice or fittings involve.

records.notes: The site is the Philly Carnival site run by the United Caribbean Association of Philadelphia, the batch name. The footer reads 2026 and the call for the 2027 band is current, but no month-dated events were listed. The Events and Gallery pages were linked but not read. Band practice dates and costume costs are not published. The nonprofit also runs some programs under fiscal sponsorship, which the site mentions but does not describe.

records.name: University City Arts League
records.summary: An art center in West Philadelphia, founded in 1967 in an old Victorian house. It offers adult and kids' art classes, memberships with open studio time, and exhibitions. Its rooms can also be rented for rehearsals, recitals and events.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for an adult art class or a kids' class (Arts After School, grades K to 5, for the 2026 to 27 school year). Members get open studio time and class discounts. Anyone can visit the gallery, and the BOHÉMIENNE show runs October 2 to 29, 2026.

schedule.text: Adult classes and workshops run by term, and the Fall 2026 term is listed. Arts After School runs during the 2026 to 27 school year. Gallery shows run for several weeks at a time.

cost.text: Classes and memberships have fees. Exact prices are on the site and were not recorded here.

first_step.how: Browse the Fall 2026 adult classes through the Take a Class link on theartsleague.org and sign up for one, or visit the gallery during the BOHÉMIENNE show before October 29.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public with online sign-up, but the site does not say whether they are for beginners.

records.notes: The address comes from the IRS listing in our batch, not the site, which did not show one. The email published on the site is for space rental questions. The adult education page (Take a Class) was linked but not read separately. Volunteer options are not mentioned on the site.

records.name: Variant 6
records.notes: A professional vocal chamber ensemble in Philadelphia. Public roles found: attend concerts (the 2026/27 season is listed with no dates or venues on the page), donate by check, sign up for the newsletter (the page carries an editor note that the form may not work yet), and send education inquiries. Education work is for college and school students, such as masterclasses and residencies, not the general public. The site mentions community-oriented projects but names none the public can join, and it lists no class, workshop, membership, volunteer or open rehearsal, so the verdict is not_a_group under the brief. If the owner wants professional ensembles listed for concert attendance, flip this to publish.

records.name: We Are the Seeds
records.summary: A Native-led arts and culture group, a project of CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia. It shares contemporary Indigenous arts through a yearly Philadelphia weekend, a listening garden, workshops, and a podcast.
records.what_you_do: Go to the Seeds Philly weekend, which has an art show, live painting, short films, workshops and artist talks. Visit the Seeds Indigenous Listening Garden in West Philadelphia. Schools and organizations can request an Indigenous arts workshop through the request form on the site.

schedule.text: Seeds Philly is a yearly weekend in September. The 2026 weekend was September 19 and 20. The listening garden is open to visit, and its details are on the gardens page, which was not read.

cost.text: Admission for the weekend is not stated on the home page.

first_step.how: Visit the Seeds Indigenous Listening Garden in West Philadelphia, or sign up for the seasonal newsletter on the site to hear when the next Seeds Philly weekend is.
first_step.basis: The garden and the weekend are open to the public, but the home page does not say when the next Seeds Philly weekend is.

records.notes: The newsletter sign-up is marked as possibly not working (it needs a storage setup), so that step may fail. Admission for the weekend is not stated. Volunteer, membership and youth options are not mentioned. The garden and workshop request pages were linked but not read. The podcast is on Podbean, Apple and Spotify. No address or phone is published, and the batch lists a PO Box, which is a mailing address only.

records.name: Three Aksha
records.summary: A dance group that teaches and performs Bharatanatyam, an Indian classical dance style. Its site lists a beginner class and past productions, but the newest dated item is from 2018.
records.what_you_do: The site lists a beginner class, but it gives no days, cost or sign-up details. Its video and gallery pages show past productions to watch.

locations.label: Address in IRS listing, not shown on site

first_step.how: Ask through the contact page on threeaksha.org whether the beginner class is running and how to join.
first_step.basis: The site says the class is for beginners, but it gives no days, cost, sign-up steps or current contact details.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the events page is April 2018 and no upcoming events are listed, so the status is dormant. The site still shows its default WordPress tagline, the beginner class page has a 'Test Class #1' heading, and the events page has an unrelated software-activation line. Treat the site as unreliable. The address comes from the IRS listing in our batch, not the site, which shows none.

records.name: Awbury Arboretum
records.summary: A nature sanctuary in Germantown, once the home of a Quaker family. The grounds are free to visit every day, and the group runs walks, children's camps, a farm and an art gallery.
records.what_you_do: Walk the grounds for free with a self-guided map, join a guided walk such as the Buckeye Harvest forage walk on October 10, 2026, or sign up a child for a camp such as School Day Off Camp. The site also links a volunteer page and a membership page.

schedule.text: The grounds are open every day from dawn to dusk. The events calendar lists 10 events from October 10, 2026 to May 17, 2027, including guided walks, camps and a harvest festival.

cost.text: The grounds are free and open to the public. Program fees were not checked.

first_step.how: Visit the grounds during the day with the free self-guided walking map, then check the events calendar for the next guided walk or camp.
first_step.basis: The grounds are free for anyone to visit and guided events are listed, but the site does not describe how drop-in walks work.

records.notes: The Farm at Awbury and several children's program pages are on a different host (awbury.wpengine.com), which looks like a staging copy, so details from those pages are unconfirmed. The volunteer and membership pages were linked but not read. The site notes a 2025 Cultural Fund grant.

records.name: Agile Rascal Theatre
records.notes: A theater company that makes bicycle-based shows. The public role found is seeing the shows: a May 2027 Philadelphia premiere is listed as in development, and Ghost Ride (2024) was in Philadelphia. The support and partners pages describe donations and funders only. No class, workshop, open rehearsal, volunteer or community program was found, so the verdict is not_a_group under the brief. The EIN on the support page (82-1376566) matches our batch. Reconsider if the contact page (not read) shows a community or education program.

records.name: BuildaBridge International
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses art making, including music, writing and painting, to help children and communities that have faced trauma. It runs youth studios and public programs, and it needs volunteers and teachers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, teach, become an ambassador or join the board through the get-involved page. Attend a public Therapeutic Percussion program, such as The Drummer's Journey, or sign up for the newsletter. The youth studios (music, writing and visual art) serve children and teens, and eligibility is not stated on the site.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Use the get-involved page to offer to volunteer or teach, or sign up for the newsletter on the contact page.
first_step.basis: Volunteering and newsletter sign-up are open to anyone, but the site lists no volunteer training dates or class schedules.

records.notes: The newest visible date is the year 2026, from the footer and a charity rating badge, with no month, so the status is probably active. The site does not list program schedules, fees, or whether programs run outside Philadelphia. The site says the Arts of Self-Care program has an adult version for caregivers. The site says it does not state who is eligible for the youth programs.

notes: Verdicts: 15 publish, 3 not_a_group (Philadelphia Dance Projects, Variant 6, Agile Rascal Theatre). Publish includes 6 records with unknown or unverified details because the site was empty, JavaScript only, blocked or an admin preview: Public Trust, Warriors of the Wonderful Sound, 2CENTS Inc, Cliveden of the National Trust, plus Three Aksha (dormant, unreliable site). Cultural Fund grantee directory (https://philaculturalfund.org/grantee-directory) is cited as the source for group existence from the batch lead ids; the directory itself was not re-fetched. Grave Gardeners (http://www.gravegardeners.org) was fetched and folded into The Woodlands record as its own volunteer program, so it is not in leads_only. Mentioned but not checked, no URL seen: Miro Dance Theatre (a Three Aksha collaborator), Green Philly and Philly Queer Birders (named on The Woodlands calendar), CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia (sponsor of We Are the Seeds). Fetches used: 49 of 60. Searches: 0 (none allowed for this agent). Budget was not exhausted.
